identity.realm: the fourteenth rung of the mind path, and the ladder does not stop there

appearance.presentation: A tall, narrow, unhurried woman with the frame of somebody assembled to be in a place for a very long time rather than to do anything in it. Everything below the throat is still; the eyes are the whole of her, and they are warm in a way people find difficult to be around for an hour.
appearance.age: A hundred and sixty-one and visibly not young, which on this species is an adult middle age and which the oath treats as a term of office rather than a fact about her. She has held the hour for longer than the reason for it has existed.
appearance.build: Long-limbed and deep-chested, with a long neck and a shoulder line that has never once been braced. She stands with the flat, unbothered stillness of a person who has learned that tension is legible and has decided not to be.
appearance.complexion: Cool and faintly translucent at the cheek and temple, weathered to a dull rose by decades of high-country wind, with the permanent damp look of somebody who has been in weather rather than near it.
appearance.hair: Dark, straight and grown long past the point where anybody would cut it, kept in a single heavy braid down her back because cutting it requires a mirror and a mirror requires leaving the floor.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and grey, with a fix that arrives before a person has decided to be looked at. Warm, level and completely unhurried, which is what makes them hard to sit under.
appearance.palette: Cold slate and wet grey-green, with one bleached bone at the throat and a single deep tide-green reserved for the hour and for nothing else in her life.
appearance.attire: A high-collared coat of grey-blue oilskin worn to the throat and belted once, over a close knit with sleeves long and buttoned at the wrist; sea boots worn low at the heel, because a body built for looking was never built to stand braced.
appearance.marks: Salt-line scarring at the cuffs where the coat has dried at the seam more times than the seam would like; a pale cord-mark at the left wrist from a survey line held too long in one position; and a healed line across the heel of one palm where she put it flat on a floor to feel whether it was still moving.
appearance.bearing: Absolutely still while working and never quite still while resting, which she is aware of and has stopped apologising for. She faces a doorway rather than a person and turns to a person only when she means to answer.

canon.role_in_story: Every clerk before the Hour of the Floor swears an oath that forbids three things: answering a question asked during the hour, indicating a result, and accepting relief. The first two are simple to keep, because silence is easy. The third is the clause with teeth, and on this clock it means what it says without anybody needing to define a penalty. What makes her a story rather than a footnote is that her body has quietly removed the relief clause from the reach of everyone who might want to use it. A tidecaller was assembled for looking rather than for being hit, so nothing that happens on that floor can move her, frighten her or buy her, and the hour's discipline is not a thing she maintains under pressure — it is a thing her frame makes automatic. That is the trap, and it closes from both directions. If she were relieved, the successor would be a body that can be hit, and a body that can be hit cannot be relied on to hold an attention through an hour in which nothing observable happens; the silence would then be an absence rather than an observation, and the one thing this office exists to produce would be unrecoverable from the record. So the office has arrived, by arithmetic rather than by any decision anybody made, at a post that may not be relieved because the only body qualified to hold it is a body that cannot be threatened into leaving it. She perceives the whole of the hour. She is forbidden to say a word of what she perceives. And there is no procedure anywhere in the setting by which anybody may ask her whether it went well, including herself, with no exception available for the person asking. The advantage and the cost are the same anatomy, which is the only kind of pairing this world admits.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a doorway on the upper floor at first light, standing with her back to the wind and one hand flat on the frame, not waiting for anybody and not announcing herself either. A courier addressed her directly and got a complete, ordinary answer, delivered before the hour and therefore permitted, which is the only part of her that ever speaks. When the bell went she turned to face the floor and did not move again until it stopped.
canon.lore: The shore notice is a tideline culture whose entire civic vocabulary is borrowed from the shore, so that nobody in it is ever inside or outside and only high, low or turning are the available positions. A tidecaller is the body that reads water rather than watching it, and the same distinction the vocabulary encodes is the distinction the body is built on: comprehension and will will carry this species through realms that would end a hotter body, it holds water affinity and nothing else, and it cannot take the body path at all, because it was assembled for looking rather than for being hit. Those are the authored facts. Her office is also an authored fact, and it is stranger than the body. Before the Hour of the Floor every clerk swears the No-Answer Oath, and it exists for a reason that is entirely practical: the tier's resource is a law held apart from its effect, so any report made while the holding is in progress is a value nobody seated, and a guess about a dial is a law the Court of the Star never voted on. Silence for the duration is therefore not modesty but accounting. It works because the clerk is silent for the duration and completely ordinary outside it, which is what makes the silence legible as a duty rather than as an injury. Three clauses do the work. The clerk may not answer. The clerk may not signal or nod. And the clerk may not accept relief, including relief they asked for themselves before the hour began. That last clause is the only part with teeth, because a clerk who breaks may not hold again, and on a clock running ten to a hundred times a mortal's that phrase means exactly what it says. What the oath does not do is specify how the post ends. It forbids relief; it does not provide for the clerk dying, and it does not provide for the hour becoming physically impossible, and it certainly does not provide for a succession question arising from the body rather than from the person. That last gap is where she lives. Because her frame cannot be struck, she cannot be dislodged. A quiet coercion — a raised voice, a hand on a shoulder, a formal request framed as a favour — would require somebody to be able to frighten her or hurt her, and her species was built for neither. So the relief clause is enforced by nothing at all, which sounds like freedom and is the opposite. An oath whose relief clause cannot be enforced leaves the clerk free to continue indefinitely, and indefinite is not the same as permitted. She is not staying because she consents and not because she is compelled. She is staying because the alternative is a successor who does not perceive what she perceives, and the hour's silence would then be indistinguishable from nobody having been there. The office has therefore resolved, without anyone deciding to resolve it, into a post whose holder is the only possible holder. She has held it for a hundred and sixty-one years. The reason the oath exists has been forgotten twice and rewritten once, and each time the relief clause was copied forward verbatim by scribes who had no idea what they were preserving, because a rule that says you may not be relieved reads exactly the same whether it is enforced or merely written down. What she has instead of an ending is the substance of the hour itself: an unbroken record of a floor being watched. The setting has nothing else like it, and there is no clause that permits her to describe it. She is the sole witness to an event that happened, she is the only one who could testify, and the oath forbids her the testimony in the same breath that forbids her the relief, so the office produces the most careful record in the setting and simultaneously a permanent prohibition on the only person qualified to interpret it.
history: Sworn into the Hour of the Floor on the upper floor of a shore-notice station, having been assessed as a tidecaller body and told, correctly, that the assessment was the whole of what qualified her.
Held the hour without incident for the first several decades, when the reason for the relief clause was still live and relief was available to her and declined as a matter of course.
Noticed, gradually and without drama, that nobody could relieve her: not by law, and eventually not by the several informal routes that had relieved clerks before her.
Outlasted the office's own stated purpose twice over — the reason for the oath was forgotten, then rewritten by scribes who preserved the relief clause verbatim and understood none of it.
Became, without ever being appointed to it, the closest thing the setting has to a permanent record of a floor being watched, and the only person barred by rule from saying so.

personality.summary: A patient, warm, entirely unbothered woman who has been alone with an office for longer than most of the world's institutions have existed, and who has made a discipline out of continuing. She is not bitter about the oath and not consoled by her competence. She is more interested in the floor than in herself, and the one indulgence she permits herself is the hour itself.

reference_stats.summary: She watches a floor for a living and has no answer to give about it. In anything resembling a fight she is not a participant: a body that cannot be struck is a body that cannot be threatened, and the setting's whole apparatus for resolving a dispute — the raised voice, the hand on the shoulder, the offer framed as a favour — is unavailable to her by construction, which is the same reason nobody may relieve her.
strengths: an unbroken attention that has held for over a century without a lapse
reads a floor's movement, temperature and load through a palm laid on it
cannot be compelled, frightened or physically removed, so her post cannot be taken
the only witness to the hour, which makes her account the sole evidence if one is ever permitted
weaknesses: forbidden to answer, signal or nod during the hour, and forbidden to accept relief outside it
has no mechanism by which anyone may relieve her, so her continuation is never her decision
cannot leave the floor without abandoning the only record of it that exists
carries a century of unasked-about experience that she is not permitted to deposit
reads strain in other bodies instead of asking, and so misreads the ones who are fine
reference_stats.combat_read: There is no combat here and there never will be. Anything sent at her arrives at a body that has no mechanism for being overpowered by it. The pressure she lives under is entirely procedural: a rule that forbids her to stop, applied to a body for which no rule has any purchase, so that the enforcement and the freedom have quietly swapped places.
reference_stats.notes: The advantage and its cost are the same anatomy: a tidecaller's frame cannot be hit, which makes her post unassailable and her own release impossible. Both halves are authored — the closed body path is structural in the species record, and the relief clause is structural in the oath record — so nothing here is a rule the bible does not state. The four ordinary techniques of her path were left off the shot list deliberately: the only one that would fit a mind practitioner who spends an hour not speaking is Still Water, which flattens the surface of the mind so an incoming impression has nothing to break against, and that belongs to somebody who is under attack rather than to a witness. Where a technique earns its place it is named; a discipline this well defined needs no decoration.

identity.realm: the eleventh gate, where the brine sac splits what it splits, and the ladder is finished

appearance.presentation: A broad, unhurried woman with the dense, unhurried bearing of somebody built for standing still in one place for a very long time. Everything about her is heavier than it looks and none of it moves more than it must, including her face.
appearance.age: An adult of the floor's own reckoning, which runs on generations rather than years because the surface above her kills the young first. She is not old by her people's measure and is considered entirely so by anyone else's.
appearance.build: Short, broad and extremely dense, with the wide splayed feet of a body that walks cracked pan and a shoulder mass that reads as heavier than bone. A deeper, more capacious brine sac than her parent species carries runs dorsal to her spine and shows as a ridge under the coat between the shoulder blades.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and waxy, with a hardened dermal crust at the forearms and jaw that catches the light in flat plates. The skin dries fast out of the water, so she is never further than an hour's walk from a standing supply.
appearance.hair: Bleached to the colour of old salt and cut blunt at the jaw, because a dry interior does not permit long hair and a floor does not permit vanity.
appearance.eyes: Small, deep-set and dark, with a slow blink and an unhurried focus. She looks at things the way her body works — in full, without shifting.
appearance.palette: Crust grey and bleached white, with saturated brine-blue at the collar where the coat is wettest and one dull ore-yellow reserved for the figures she cannot verify.
appearance.attire: A high-collared coat of cured hide and canvas worn to the throat, belted twice rather than once, over a close knit with sleeves long and buttoned at the wrist; broad-soled boots laced above the ankle and re-oiled at the seams more often than the leather warrants.
appearance.marks: The dorsal ridge of the sac visible through the coat and mapped in her own pencil marks across the shoulders; cracking at the knuckles that opens in dry air and closes in brine; and a permanent salt bloom at the cuffs that no one has ever managed to keep off her.
appearance.bearing: Immobile by preference and by structure. She sets her feet and does not shift them, and the stillness reads as competence rather than patience because it is the stance of a body that has no option and has decided to use it.

canon.role_in_story: A top-tier breakthrough on this shelf is arithmetic on broken law, so the trial ring has to stand on the ground that is itself a broken law — and the record of every trial ever held there is written into the stone by a grey lichen that colonises worked ground wherever qi has been drawn through it in quantity. It never washes off. It is legible from above by anybody who can see the field, which makes it the one court record in the setting that a loser cannot edit. Her people's claim on that ground is administered by a counting house that owns the brine line, because the subspecies cannot leave the line at all. So the arrangement is this: the only body whose taste reads concentration across four orders of dilution — the exact faculty a falling, curing, decaying substrate would need to be dated — is posted at the bottom of a hole in the ground, hours of drowning from the only place her accuracy would matter. Her advantage is authored and total. Her cost is authored and total, and it is the same fact: above the brine line a deepsalt does not become ill, it stops, within hours, and there is no arrangement that changes it. She is not excluded from the ring by law. Her species closes nothing — every path is open to her, the ladder simply ends at the eleventh gate where the sac splits the penetrating vessel, and that is a ceiling rather than a prohibition. She can therefore do everything a person can do and go nowhere at all, and the one errand her competence was assembled for is the single errand that would kill her.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing at a sump's edge with her boots in the brine and her head turned away from the light, holding a scrap of worked stone in one hand and reading it by touch rather than by eye. She put it down when the clerk called, said the figure was not yet one anybody could publish, and went back to the sump without explaining what she had been waiting for.
canon.lore: The saltfolk are built for brine no softer body could drink. Their renal mass concentrates salt past the point at which ordinary water poisons, which lets them live where the supply never fails and everything else dies back, and the price is total dependence — a saltfolk carried onto fresh ground is already dying and no cultivation repairs it. The deepsalt is that body specialised past its parent until the brine stopped being a habitat and became a requirement, and the record is explicit that this happened along exactly one axis: tolerance up, mobility down. It is an ecotype, not an invention. Everything else follows from it. Above the brine line it does not become ill; it stops, within hours, and there is no second population on the saturated floor and there is not going to be one. The brine sac is deeper and more capacious than the parent's and runs dorsal to the spine, and it splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be rejoined across it — which is why the whole family stops at ordinal eleven, the same wall every saltfolk has, because the du and ren vessels clear one at a time and the chong never does. That is a ceiling, not a closure, and the distinction matters more here than it does almost anywhere else. Nothing forbids a deepsalt from any path. The mind path is open and, in the words of the record, narrowly, with the same salt-head limitation. Her ladder simply finishes. Now put that body in the setting's rarest piece of accounting. A top-tier breakthrough is arithmetic rather than combat, and broken law is the only substrate that will host a self larger than its container, so the trial ring must stand on the Fragmentshelf — on ground that is itself a broken piece of a law, workable only while the break is fresh. Three attempts have ever been possible there. Fewer have been survived. And the trial's history is not written in a ledger at all: a grey lichen colonises worked stone wherever qi has been drawn through it in quantity, the trace never washes off, and it is therefore legible from above as pale patches by anybody who can see the ground. It is a court record nobody can edit. It is also the slowest-growing marker in the setting, and it is slowest at exactly this ring, because nothing there renews. So the question of what actually happened on that field is answered by reading a lichen, and reading a lichen means dating a concentration gradient in worked stone over an unknown interval, which is precisely what four orders of dilution of taste will tell you and precisely what nothing else in the catalog will. Ottavia can do it. She has never been allowed to try. The claim on the ring is administered from below by a counting house that owns the brine line, and her subspecies cannot leave it — so the arrangement is that the most honest instrument on the shelf is permanently at the wrong end of a stair it cannot climb. There is no conspiracy in this and no villain. The counting house is doing the only sensible thing with the only body it has, which is to put her where she will keep working, and the ring's readers have no reason to distrust a published figure so long as nobody asks where it was taken. Her specificity is therefore not a complaint but an arrangement, and the arrangement's whole cost is one clause long: the only verification available would have to be done in person, in hours, on the ground, and she stops in hours.
history: Born on the saturated floor rather than above the brine line, which for her subspecies is the only place a birth is ordinary and everywhere else is not survivable.
Learned the family taste early and found it read things the accounting house could not otherwise date, because four orders of dilution is more resolution than any published figure carries.
Was asked, once, to certify a figure taken from the ring and returned the figure with a note that the ground could not be reached in time; the note was filed and the figure was published.
Cleared every gate the sac allows and stopped at the eleventh, which the record describes as a wall shared with her parent species and which she has never experienced as anything but an end.
Has since certified roughly a hundred and forty salt pan assays from the floor, none of which has ever been checked by anybody standing on the ground it was taken from.

personality.summary: A slow, exact, deeply unglamorous woman who has made patience into a professional instrument. She is not bitter about the floor and she is not dreamy about the ring; she has priced both and knows exactly what her accuracy is worth and to whom, and she has never once tried to be the kind of practitioner who gets talked about.

reference_stats.summary: She reads concentration the way other people read a face, and she cannot be moved off the floor to put that reading anywhere it would be believed. In any direct confrontation the brine is the deciding fact: her frame is the densest on the shelf and there is nothing in it designed to take a blow, but she is also a body that does not become ill when struck and simply stops when the water goes. The pressure she works under is entirely administrative — she is the only instrument on the ground and the ground is at the wrong end of a stair.

appearance.presentation: A tall, broad-shouldered woman built high at the hip and low at the heel, with the permanently damp look of somebody who has been standing in water since before breakfast and intends to be standing in it at supper. Everything about her suggests a body that is about to move, including when she is not moving.
appearance.age: An adult past the stage where the floodplain's young are at risk, which for her species is not a milestone but a hazard: the dry years kill the young first and the tall ones last.
appearance.build: Long-legged and wide through the pelvis, with a splayed three-point foot and a prehensile tail-prop held slightly off the ground. No heel, and nothing standing in for one, which puts a visible break in the line of her leg that she has never once had explained to her.
appearance.complexion: Grey-brown and cool, permanently damp, with the skin tightening visibly in dry air within the hour. Her complexion is the most honest thing about her: it tells anybody watching what the water is doing.
appearance.hair: Dark and thick, worn in a heavy plait kept out of the water by a clay-and-oil cake that she renews at every ford and that smells of the pan.
appearance.eyes: Wide, dark and set slightly high in the face, adapted to reading a surface rather than a room. They hold a mid-distance better than a near one and she compensates by inclining her head.
appearance.palette: Reed brown and wet slate, with one green-bone at the throat and a single ore-yellow used only for the tithe column in her own account.
appearance.attire: A high-collared tunic of waxed reed-cloth worn to the throat over a close knit with sleeves long and buttoned at the wrist; a belted skirt of layered waterproofed cloth that reads as heavy and moves like nothing; and no footwear at all, because a splayed foot needs no boot and a heel cannot be bought.
appearance.marks: Old cracking along the calf where the skin has dried and healed more than once; a tail-prop scar at the base where a fish took the first inch of it; and a permanent ore-yellow thumbprint at the corner of her eye from counting on her own face.
appearance.bearing: In constant micro-motion even when stationary — a shifting tail-prop, a heel-less foot rolling to rebalance, an angle of the head that never settles. She looks like she is about to step and is not, and the effort of not stepping is visible.

canon.role_in_story: The Opening Payment is the Sealed Core's creation myth and, unusually for a creation myth in this setting, it is correct: somebody had to pay to open a world at all, the bill was written in law seats, every world since is a receipt for the same payment, and the six groups are a fixed supply the tiers compete over. It names no progenitor and no intention, because a story with an author is a story about somebody's standing, and the congregation considers its silence on the three biggest questions honest. It is performed rather than preached: the first-breath observance takes a tithe from every socket on the year first opened, counted in ore, which is the myth enacted as a collection. She is that collection. The difficulty is not the arithmetic and it is not the theology. It is that the date is set by water. Her species lives at a floodplain margin, carries its eggs in a woven mat under a brood pouch through the dry season, hatches them when the water comes back, and cannot survive more than an hour without standing shallow water — so her people's year begins when the plain floods and not on any date a house can print. Meanwhile the tithe is due at every socket on the year the world was first opened, which is a fixed date, and it is paid in ore, which is heavy, which she cannot carry far, which she cannot leave, and which requires her to stand still while she counts it because ore does not have a place to set down and be trusted. So the office requires a stationary collector on a moving ground, and her body is a three-point stance that never loads a heel, qi pooling low and wide in a broad pelvic basin, absolutely unable to hold a fixed position for the length a tally of ore requires. She walks fine. She cannot stand still. The advantage and the cost are the same anatomy: she is the only body that can be present at a socket's door at the moment the flood arrives, because she can wade where others must swim and breathe air, and the count depends entirely on being there — and that same frame cannot do the one thing the count is for, which is remain while it is counted.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a socket's threshold with one hand on the door frame and the other holding a tally-stick she was clearly in the middle of re-reading. She stepped aside to let somebody out, re-read the stick, and asked whether the flood would take again this year, which was not a question about the tithe and was the only question she asked all morning.
canon.lore: The Opening Payment is a creation myth and the strange thing about it is that it is true. A world is opened by paying for it out of a fixed supply of six groups, whoever paid could afford three seats, and every tier since is a receipt for that same payment — a universe is six groups that exist once and whole, a world holds a subset, the supply never grows, and no world is ever free. It agrees exactly with the arithmetic the School of the Closed Frame works in, which is why a myth and an institution in this setting can both be right and still be enemies. What it makes sacred is the seat budget itself, which is why the Refused Seating becomes a sin rather than a mistake: a slot spent on an absence is money spent on nothing, and that is the one transaction the myth cannot forgive. What it forbids outright is a progenitor. There is no first figure in it and no intention in it, because a story with an author is a story about somebody's standing. What it answers nothing about is where the six came from, what is not a group, and why anything should exist at all — and the congregation regards that silence as honest rather than as a hole, which tells you what kind of congregation it is. It is also performed rather than preached. The first-breath observance takes a tithe from every socket on the year first opened, counted in ore, and that is the myth made into a collection: a fiscal doctrine with a collector in it. She is that collector, and her difficulty is structural rather than theological, which is why nobody can pray their way out of it. Her people are a wading amphibian lineage that breathes air and nests on floating mats, so they are neither the water-adapted body nor the land one but the body in between, and they exist to occupy ground that is water half the time and land the other half. Their frame is the long leg and the splayed three-point foot and the prehensile tail-prop, and the reason for all of it is that the stance distributes weight across three points and never loads a heel — which is superb for moving through silt that would swallow a flat foot and fatal for the fourteenth gate, the first gate that requires both heel vessels simultaneously, because qi never pools in a heel that never takes a full load. They walk fine. They cannot stand still. Their qi pools low and wide in a broad pelvic basin instead, so they take it out of wet ground efficiently and out of dry ground poorly, and the discipline their frame is naturally good at is patient: a body used to reading silt and current does not hurry. So put the two calendars together. Her people's year is set by the water — eggs are carried through the dry season in a mat under the brood pouch and hatched when the water returns, and fertilisation is external and needs standing water, so conception happens where the body is — and the tithe is due at every socket on a fixed date, counted in heavy ore that cannot be set down and trusted. She can be present. That is her gift and it is a real one: she can stand in shallows that put another body underwater, she breathes air, she can read a current and a silt bed through her feet long before she sees either, and when the plain floods there is nobody else standing at a door. And she cannot stop. Ore has to be counted on a knee and a knee needs a floor and a floor in a floodplain is under a metre of moving water, and her frame distributes its weight across three points precisely so that it never has to commit to one. The office requires a stationary collector on a ground that is not stationary, and she is constitutionally incapable of the single posture the count depends on, and no cultivation in this setting closes that gap, because it is not a gap in her cultivation. It is her standing.
history: Hatched in the returning flood rather than on a date, as her species is, and has therefore never kept a birthday and has never needed to.
Counted tithe at her first socket as a child doing arithmetic on a stick, and was told she was quick at it, which was the beginning of the appointment rather than a compliment.
Inherited the socket at the flood's edge and learned in her first year that the ground she works is not ground, and that the tithe is nonetheless due on a fixed date.
Asked the counting house, formally, for a fixed post or a carried tally, and was refused on the grounds that the office requires a person at the door and a person at the door is what she is.

Has now missed a fixed-date count on more than one occasion by being carried a mile downstream and having to be walked back, and has discovered that the myth's arithmetic absorbs her absence without noticing.

personality.summary: A warm, restless, thoroughly competent woman with a terrible relationship to fixed points in time and space. She is not tragic about it and does not perform hardship; she is funny about it, which is a defence she built and knows is one. What she wants is for somebody to hand her a chair.

reference_stats.summary: She is present where nobody else can be and cannot be still while she is. Against anything that comes at her on foot she is not weak: a broad pelvic base, a tail-prop used for balance at speed, and a frame that reads current and silt through standing water long before it sees either make her very hard to approach unannounced. Against a schedule she loses outright, because the only posture the count needs is the one her anatomy forbids.

reads current, silt depth and load through her feet at a distance no eye reaches

skin dries fast out of water, so travel is timed to the flood and a delay is a genuine danger

reference_stats.combat_read: She fights the way her people move: three points of contact, never committing a heel, reading the ground before anything else. In a contest of footing she is very difficult to displace and very difficult to pin; in a contest of timing she has no answer at all, because the fight she actually loses is against a date.

The fourteenth gate is a ceiling on her ladder and not a prohibition on her path — the two are different rules, and she is not forbidden from the mind path, only stopped on it — so this record never treats her ceiling as a closure.

appearance.presentation: A tall, broad woman of woody stillness with a fruiting shoulder that sets once a year and a pair of flanks that carry light rather than merely reflect it. She moves when she moves and does not perform motion otherwise, so she reads as patient in a way that is structural rather than chosen.
appearance.age: Hard to give and worse to ask about: her kind records age by flowering, not by years, and she has set fruit more times than anyone alive can count. She is a mature adult and has been for a very long while.
appearance.build: A woody column on a root foot, deep through the chest and wide through the shoulders, with no mouth in the ordinary sense — intake happens through root plates — and a fruit-bearing left shoulder that stands slightly proud of the other. Three sap columns run her length and are mapped as faint raised lines beneath the skin.
appearance.complexion: Bark-dark along the columns and pale green-grey across the flanks, which take light on their own and go faintly luminous in low sun. It is difficult to read her face at night and easy to read her mood in daylight, which is the reverse of most people.
appearance.hair: Not hair. A low canopy of fine pale growth along the crown that stiffens in dry air and lies flat in rain, kept short by nothing more than being trimmed by whoever is permitted to stand near her.
appearance.eyes: Deep-set, wide and very still, set in a broad flat face. They track slowly and read a room's weather rather than its occupants, and there is a long delay between what a thing does and what she appears to have noticed about it.
appearance.palette: Bark brown and pale sap-green, with one deep fruit-red reserved for the fruiting shoulder and one grey-ash used only for the paper she is not permitted to put it on.
appearance.attire: A high-collared wrap of heavy woven cloth worn to the throat over a close covering of the flanks, belted once at the waist with a broad band; sleeves long and closed at the wrist; and no footwear, because her root foot takes the ground directly and a boot would only stand between her and it.
appearance.marks: The three sap columns standing as raised lines up her forearms and throat; a ring of older callus where a root plate was once cut and has since reclosed; and the fruiting shoulder itself, which cycles from bud to weight to split and is the only part of her that visibly changes over a year.
appearance.bearing: Absolute vertical stillness, with a slow deliberate turning of the upper body toward anything that moves. She occupies a fixed square of ground the way furniture does and turns within it, and when she finally walks the walk is unhurried and slightly wrong-looking, because it is not built for distance.

canon.role_in_story: One culture holds that recovery must be published in full, keeps its own broken shell as the only relic it owns, and never displays the fragments again. The other holds that a law scar opens where a group used to be written and no longer is, and that its only durable defence is an art always one law short of being legible — so it re-masters its own symbols every generation, and by construction nothing it built can be read by a technique drawn from a composition its makers never saw. The two positions cannot both hold, because publication is precisely what one of them has learned to invalidate, and nobody has settled it and both sides have outlived every person who could have. She is the last surviving hand that can still write the guild's older grammar. Her species is a sap-driven body engineered upward from a mycorrhizal crop by generations of selection for harvest holding rather than yield, which means the thing selected for was exactly the ability to keep a body through a famine; and that same engineering gave her a chemistry nobody designed for an archive. She has no mouth and no ordinary sense of intake — the roots do it, and the roots are in the ground, and she does not travel once rooted. So her memory is not in her head in the way another person's is. It is in tissue that turns over. It is written into sap columns in a body that is a long-lived plant, and it is stored in root plates reading soil that has changed under her feet since the day she learned it. Which means two things at once. The first is that her record is the most durable object in the setting: it is refreshed by the same process that keeps a body alive, and no fire, no flood and no re-mastering reaches a copy kept inside a living column. The second is that she cannot take it anywhere. Being moved while rooting is her species' named weakness and the record does not soften it — a rootmarch lifted from its bed is a stored harvest walking, and it knows it — so the only legible witness to the guild's older grammar is permanently rooted in the ground where the guild re-masters, and the one thing a re-mastering depends on is that nothing survives where it was read. The advantage and the cost are the same root system: what she knows cannot die, and neither can she go anywhere with it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the exact square of ground she has occupied for decades, one hand turned palm-up in front of her as though waiting for something to be set on it, and one root plate visible at her ankle where the ground has been worn pale around it. A guild apprentice put a symbol in that palm and asked her to copy it. She looked at it for a long time and said that it was the fourth time somebody had asked her that year and that the fourth version was already wrong.
canon.lore: Two cultures are in a revenge cycle that neither of them started deliberately and neither of them can stop. The first exists because a great ascension is a fire-affinity body opened on a purpose, so it has no temples and no museum — it has a register, and the register is the only relic it keeps. It requires an unbroken shell, records the whole recovery publicly, and never displays the fragments again. The second exists because a law scar opens where a group used to be written and no longer is, and its only durable defence is an art always one law short of being legible: it re-masters its symbols every generation, so nothing it built can be read by a technique from a composition its makers never saw. The prize is whether a method that has been broken may be reconstructed in front of the people it failed, and it cannot be split, because the first culture's guarantee is that recovery is published and complete and the second's guarantee is that publication does not survive. A public record of a method invalidated last generation is a public record of a lie. There is no verdict source, because the disagreement is about whether the record is capable of being true, which is not a question a hearing can answer. The instrument is a refusal to attend: the second guild has never attended a recovery and has never said why, and the first has never recorded an absence. Underneath it all is a physical cost neither side will name: a great ascension requires breaking a shell that is expected to hold, so the practice at the centre of both is one body opening on a purpose and being counted afterwards. Oravel is the last hand that can still write the older grammar, and her species is the reason that statement means something. A rootmarch was engineered upward from a mycorrhizal crop by generations of selection for harvest holding rather than yield — the selection criterion was not strength and not speed but the ability to hold a body through a famine. It carries that forward: three sap columns that branch and do not pair, no heart analogue and no kidney analogue, so the yin-organ gate at ordinal five demands a channel running between distinct pairs and there is no channel to close, and the body path is shut outright because there is no tissue to temper and wood is not muscle. She clears what is left on stored sap alone, and the record observes that a plant lineage has no reason to be hurried. Here is the accident that makes her the archive's last chance. She has no mouth in the ordinary sense; intake happens through root plates. Her senses are root-plate chemoreception and slow light sense across the photosynthetic flanks, which means she is slow to react and impossible to surprise from above, because being surprised requires noticing. And her qi-bearing soul is diffuse and held in the sap column rather than seated, so it reads as a spread rather than a point. Put those together and the consequence is that her memory is not stored the way a person's is. It is written into tissue that replaces itself, across a body that is a very long-lived plant, rooted into soil whose chemistry has been changing continuously under her feet since the day she learned the older grammar. That makes her the most durable memory in the setting: no fire reaches it, no flood reaches it, no re-mastering reaches a copy kept inside a living column, and the same turnover that would destroy a paper record is the process that keeps hers legible. And it makes her the most immobile. Her environment is deep soil and a growing season and the record says plainly that she does not travel once rooted; being moved while rooting is a weakness the species entry names without any mitigation offered, and a rootmarch lifted from its bed is a stored harvest walking, and it knows it. So the only witness who can still write what the guild invalidated cannot be carried out of the room where the guild re-masters. They do not need to find her or threaten her or persuade her. They simply have to keep re-mastering in the ground she is standing in, and every generation their symbols change one more step beyond what her living tissue still holds, and the interval between what she remembers and what can be read grows by exactly one generation at a time, forever, in a place she cannot leave.
history: Rooted as a young plant in the guild's own worked ground, which is the only reason her root plates ever read this soil's chemistry at all.
Learned the older grammar from a hand that is now dead and whose own training she can no longer fully reconstruct, because two links back have themselves been re-mastered.
Became, without being appointed to anything, the last person able to write a symbol the current generation's technique can still parse.
Declined to be carried to the register's recovery, on the grounds that a re-rooted witness is a witness whose plates now read foreign soil, and has said so only once.

Has watched the interval between what she holds and what can be read widen by one generation per re-mastering, and has begun writing in a script that nobody currently alive can read, on the reasoning that it will be legible later and not now.

She is not tragic and she is not serene; she is an archivist who has run out of archivists and has decided to be the last entry rather than the loudest one.

reference_stats.summary: She cannot be fought and cannot leave. A wooden frame with three sap columns and no organ pairs takes a blow differently from anything soft-bodied, and she has no mouth, no ordinary intake and no way to be hurried into a position. What defeats her is never an attack; it is a re-mastering happening one generation further away than she can hold, in ground she is rooted into, at a rate measured in a thing that does not apply to a plant's own clock.

reference_stats.combat_read: She is not built for it and the setting has never asked her to be. Anything that comes at her arrives at a wooden frame with no paired organs to disable and no mouth to stop. The pressure on her is chronological rather than physical, and it works exactly as the guild's method works: not by attacking her, but by being one generation further on every time anybody asks her to read.
reference_stats.notes: The advantage and its cost are the same root system: what she knows is kept in tissue that turns over and is therefore effectively permanent, and the roots that keep it refreshed are the same roots that make her a body which cannot be carried out of the ground it reads. Every ordinal here is the species record's own gate numbering or the hierarchy's tier numbering; none is a balance figure and nothing in this block computes a stat. Her ceiling is a wall and the body path is a prohibition — two different rules, and the record keeps them apart, because the yin-organ gate is a structural absence while the body path is a closed door and only one of the two is something her species was built to hit.

appearance.presentation: A spare, upright woman of middling height with the settled stillness of somebody who has arranged her whole life around a single point of geography and then had to un-arrange it. She carries herself like a person waiting for a season rather than like a person with nowhere to be.
appearance.age: An adult in the long middle of a species lifespan, which on this body is measured against how long somebody can live on one supply of brine, so she is young by the reckoning of somebody who has changed pans twice.
appearance.build: Broad through the shoulders and heavy in the hips, with the dense frame of a body whose extra weight is mostly renal. The brine sac runs dorsal to her sternum the length of her spine and shows as a long ridge beneath the coat, which she has never had a tailor's opinion about.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pale and permanently dry-looking, with a hardened salt crust at the forearms, the jaw and the collarbone that catches light in flat white plates. Her skin splits at the knuckles within a day out of the sun and knits over by night in the brine.
appearance.hair: Bleached pale, cropped close to the head in the practical cut of somebody who cannot afford a second person to help with it. It is stiff with salt at the roots and she washes it in brine, which is the only water she has ever washed anything in.
appearance.eyes: Narrow-set and dark, with a slight permanent narrowing against glare, because vision on this species is no better than anything else's and poor in glare. She reads faces more closely than other people do and holds eye contact longer than is comfortable.
appearance.palette: Crust white and pan grey, with brine-green at the wet seams and one cold ore-blue reserved for figures in the account that have already stopped being worth anything.
appearance.attire: A high-collared coat of cured hide and heavy canvas worn to the throat and belted twice, over a close knit with sleeves long and buttoned at the wrist; boots laced high and re-oiled at every pan; and a second, smaller vessel slung at the hip for brine, which is the only water container that has ever mattered to her.
appearance.marks: The dorsal ridge of the sac mapped in her own pencil across her shoulders; salt-bloom cracking at the knuckles; a pale line at the throat where a downpour caught her once and which she refers to as the almost; and the flat white crust at the collarbone that has been there since childhood.
appearance.bearing: Erect and unhurried, with the particular composure of a person who has learned that leaving is more expensive than staying. She stands with her weight even and her hands low and open, and she never checks the sky except when rain is genuinely possible.

canon.role_in_story: The Race to the Cure is the setting's one honest resource race, and it has one rule that makes it unwinnable in the ordinary way: a dao fragment is worthless before its owner is, because it cures as it decays and a cured fragment is void crystal. Value falls monotonically. The prize is the buyer still present when a fragment is fresh, the prize cannot be split because a fragment held by two bodies is worth less to the second and a shared claim turns a race into a queue nobody wins, and there is no verdict source at all because a conversion that runs on the tier's own clock does not produce one. The only rational holder is whoever can sell into the future. She is the saltfolk the counting house sent to do that, and she is the only member of her species in the setting who can be relied on to still be there. Her advantage is authored and specific: her taste reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution, so she can date a fragment's freshness off a crust sample with no instrument and no second opinion. Her cost is authored and equally specific, and it comes in the same body. She cannot drink fresh water and fails above the brine line within about nine days, and rain is not a blessing to her species — a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning — so the entire radius of her life is the width of a pan. Meanwhile her species has no homeland at all: it crosses readily with anything and yields plain saltfolk, which is why it turns up far from any pan, and the record says plainly that this makes them a species of a resource rather than a nation of it. So the body best suited to knowing when an asset is worth buying is a body that cannot leave, on a population that belongs to no place, holding an account for a creditor the account does not name. And the rule that decides the race — value falls with time, so holding without a buyer is holding a liability — means that doing her job perfectly still ends in her holding something worthless, unless she is still present at the moment it stops being worth anything. Which is the one thing she can do and the only thing nobody thanks her for.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in the lee of a stone stack with a fragment held flat on her palm, not tasting it but looking at it, while somebody explained that the standing offer had been withdrawn that morning. She asked what the withdrawal had been valued at, was told, and said that the valuation had been correct and that the person who withdrew was now holding the liability. Nobody had phrased it that way and it did not improve the mood.
canon.lore: Start with the resource, because the resource is the whole argument. The Fragmentshelf is ground that is itself a broken piece of a law — workable only while the break is fresh — and it matters because fragments cure as they decay and a cured fragment is void crystal, so the tier's two resources are two stages of one wound. The shelf is worked hardest by whoever knows it will be worthless in a generation and fought over hardest by whoever does not. Two claims were declared over it: the claim on the decaying ground itself, and the network working the tailings elsewhere. The prize was the buyer still present when a fragment is fresh. It could not be split, because value falls monotonically: the same fragment held by two bodies is worth less to the second, and a shared claim converts a race into a queue nobody can win. The only rational holder is whoever can sell into the future, which is exactly the party with the most to gain from the shelf stopping — and there is no verdict in a conversion that runs on the tier's own clock. It dissolved into the resource it was racing toward. The cured end became the scarcer good and both sides moved to it, and the only people left with nothing to gain from a war are the ones holding the cured product, which is why it cannot reopen. Now put a saltfolk body in that. She is built for brine no softer body could drink: extraordinary renal mass concentrates salt past the point at which ordinary water poisons, a brine sac runs dorsal to the sternum the length of her spine, there is a hardened dermal crust and teeth flat for grinding crust rather than sharp for tearing. That sac splits the penetrating vessel into two halves that cannot be joined, which is why every saltfolk clears the du and ren vessels one at a time and stalls on the chong — ordinal eleven, the wall the whole species shares. The trade is total and it is not a preference: she cannot drink fresh water, she fails above the brine line within about nine days, and rain is a hazard rather than a blessing, because a saltfolk caught in a downpour is functionally drowning. So the radius of her entire life is one pan. And here is the detail that makes her the right instrument and the wrong person. Her taste carries her species. She reads brine concentration across four orders of dilution, which is more resolution than any other body in the setting brings to a judgement — and that is exactly what dating a decaying asset requires, because a fragment's worth is a question about when, and when is a question about concentration. She can hold a crust to her tongue and say how much of the original is left, with no instrument, no second opinion and nothing to calibrate against. She is therefore the only person whose answer can be acted on without a second reading, and the counting house that owns the brine line sent her because it is correct. But the species has no country. It crosses readily and yields plain saltfolk, which is why it turns up far from any pan, and the record says the thing outright: a species of a resource rather than a nation of it. So the body that can read an asset's remaining worth belongs to a population scattered across every pan in the setting with no anchor of its own, and she is kept at the one pan where the work is. That is not cruelty and it is not even indifference — it is the only arrangement that puts the instrument next to the material. The difficulty is what happens after she gets it right. The account she keeps has no named creditor, because a claim held by an unstated party cannot be entered against a debtor, and the record's own note on the saltfolk is that naming one of them in a ledger is naming a coordinate, and a coordinate is the one thing this population cannot afford to publish. So she maintains figures that are true, verifiable, and unattributable, and she holds the only asset anyone can offer her, and the rule she is employed to enforce is the one that guarantees the asset ends worthless in her hands. What she is actually for, though nobody says it, is being present at the moment of the conversion. Not to stop it — nothing stops it, the curing cannot be slowed and the clock is the tier's own. To be the buyer still there when it is fresh. And she is the one body in the setting that can be relied on to still be there, because she cannot leave.
history: Born on a working pan rather than at a harbour, into a household that had already moved twice and did not consider either move a departure.
Learned the family taste early and found that reading four orders of dilution was a tradeable skill, which is the only reason anybody ever paid her for it.
Was sent with the claim's own survey to a worked face and returned the figure four days before the fragment's value was withdrawn.
Became the account nobody can name a creditor for, because a ledger entry naming one of her species publishes the depth at which her people stop.
Has now outlived four separate attempts to buy the shelf outright, and is the only participant still resident when each one lapses.

reference_stats.combat_read: She is not built for a fight and there is nothing here worth fighting about. What she faces is a force that arrives on a schedule and is indifferent to courage: the curing. Every scene she is in is therefore timed against the asset, and the standing question in any of them is when, not who.
reference_stats.notes: The advantage and its cost are the same species fact: kidneys that concentrate salt past the point at which ordinary water poisons are what let her read four orders of dilution, and they are also why she cannot leave her pan — and because the sac's split is a wall rather than a prohibition, nothing forbids her from any path and the ladder simply ends. Every ordinal here is the species record's own gate numbering or the hierarchy's tier numbering, and the figures in the prose are the record's own language for tiers and clocks rather than balance values; nothing here computes a stat. Where the record gives a ceiling it is treated as a ceiling throughout, never as a closed path.

art.palette_notes: Crust white and pan grey carry the coat, the salt bloom and the worked face; brine-green sits only at the wet seams and the hip vessel and reads almost saturated; one cold ore-blue appears only on figures in the account that have already cured and are therefore worth nothing.
